radiology_report:
OLVG Amsterdam | Radiology Division | 28 January 2025
Study: Multiparametric MRI of the prostate
Rationale: Evaluation of a 11.8 ng/mL prostate-specific antigen level and a prior biopsy bucket "Positive".
Observations:
The gland occupies a 61.0 mL volume. T2 sequences highlight a poorly demarcated hypointense focus in the right mid-peripheral zone, spanning roughly 14 by 12 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction, mirrored by corresponding ADC hypointensity. Post-contrast phases demonstrate prompt, localized enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Seminal vesicles remain intact. Capsular boundaries are preserved without suspicious nodal enlargement. Pelvic organs including the bladder and rectum appear unremarkable.
Conclusion:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 61.0 mL; PSA density 0.19 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.727.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review documented ongoing prostate-specific antigen elevation, registering 8.5 ng/mL in September 2023 following a 9.7 ng/mL baseline in January. Infectious workup yielded negative urinalysis and culture results, and antibiotic therapy was omitted due to absent symptomatic indicators. A urology consultation was arranged to facilitate further diagnostic evaluation and multiparametric imaging.
